solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heart complaint troubling inspector again

indicators.note: troubling signals that the letters of the two words are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A heart problem keeps bothering an inspector a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubling' shuffles INSPECTOR AGAIN, fourteen letters, into the two-word medical term.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term names chest pain caused by poor blood supply to the heart muscle, a cardiac complaint.

clue.text: Flying Officer Clive, with a hair out of place, orbiting planet

indicators.note: orbiting means the jumbled letters circle round the planet, which sits inside them
out of place says the letters of Clive and a hair are jumbled

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun

explanation.surface: An RAF officer named Clive with an untidy hairdo is circling a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying Officer' is also a real RAF rank, a junior one; here it simply means an officer of the air force, and the answer is a far more senior rank.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a senior rank in the Royal Air Force, so its holder is literally an officer who flies.

clue.text: Spice Girl has a vocally deceptive device that's aged a lot

parts.note: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls pop group

indicators.note: vocally says the word for a deceptive device is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a trick is a deceptive device or ruse

explanation.surface: A pop star owns a talking gadget for fooling people that has worn very badly.
explanation.walkthrough: TRICK spoken aloud gives the ending TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric is used loosely of someone or something very old, having aged a great deal.

clue.text: Number given in exchange

parts.note: the letters XC sit inside the word exchange, and XC is the Roman numeral for this number

explanation.surface: A figure handed over as part of a swap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' contains the run of letters X and C; read as a Roman numeral XC is 90, which is written out in full as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a cardinal number, ten less than a hundred.

clue.text: See 1
Applaud after openings of riffs in concert held by school musician

indicators.note: held by means the following pieces go inside the school name

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: after places the word for applaud behind the opening letters
openings of picks the first letter of each of the words riffs, in and concert

parts.note: to applaud is to clap

explanation.surface: Clapping follows the first notes of guitar riffs at a school gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts both the opening letters and the clapping inside the school's name, so the school splits round them rather than coming at one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Clapton is the celebrated English rock and blues guitarist, a musician famed for his riffs.

clue.text: Part of canteen providing meal at old club

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
a spoon was an old wooden golf club with a lofted face

explanation.surface: A works canteen supplies a meal at an old social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canteen' here is a canteen of cutlery, a boxed set of knives, forks and spoons, not a dining room.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen of cutlery is a boxed set of tableware, and a small stirring utensil is one item in it.

clue.text: Animal sporting one horn?

indicators.note: sporting, in the sense of playful or frolicking, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A beast with a single horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' looks like 'wearing'; it is the anagram signal shuffling I and HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a large thick-skinned African and Asian mammal.

clue.text: Sin coming before a fall, we hear — one tried in a magistrate's court

definitions.text: one tried in a magistrate's court

indicators.note: we hear says the first word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: fall is autumn, and what comes before it is summer, so summery
a sin is an offence

explanation.surface: A sin precedes a fall, as the proverb about pride goes, followed by a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'summery offence' is a sin committed in the season before fall (autumn); spoken, it gives the legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: In English law a minor crime dealt with by magistrates without a jury is given this name.

clue.text: Eager beaver finally joins a band

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word beaver

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic beaver at last joins a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eager beaver' reads as one phrase, but 'Eager' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means keen and impatient to start.

clue.text: Element of hesitation after Queen docked

indicators.note: after puts the hesitation sound at the end
docked means the queen's name has its tail cut off

parts.note: Titania is the queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A trace of hesitation after the monarch has been cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' removes the final A of TITANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a strong light metallic chemical element, number 22.

clue.text: Extended offer from McDonald's one tracked on Amazon?

parts.note: McDonald's has the letters C and D within it, offering them, and those letters extended into full words give the abbreviation spelled out

explanation.surface: A long-running promotion from the burger chain is tracked down on a shopping website.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters CD sit in McDonald's; 'extended' writes the abbreviation CD out in full. The question mark flags that 'tracked' means having tracks, and Amazon sells them.
explanation.definitionFit: A music disc has tracks and is the sort of item sold by an online retailer like Amazon.

clue.text: Back from Lugano? It can involve working

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about returning from the Swiss lakeside town, which might mean getting a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters NOITCANI within 'Lugano? It can involve'; 'Back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in action means being active and operating, as a machine that is working.

clue.text: Lack of breath an ape suffers when without oxygen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the jumbled letters surround the oxygen symbol
suffers signals that the letters of an ape are put through distress and rearranged

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A monkey struggles to breathe when deprived of oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside': APNEA, from AN APE, goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Apnoea is the medical term for a temporary stop in breathing, as in sleep apnoea.

clue.text: See 5
Almost too soon for the equivalent to count

indicators.note: Almost means the word drops its final letter

parts.note: early means too soon, before the right time

explanation.surface: It is nearly too soon to make a comparable count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like the verb to tally; it is the European nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A British earl ranks as the counterpart of a continental count.

clue.text: Disturbed sleep? Try and look back at end of day's potholing

indicators.note: Disturbed says the letters of sleep are thrown into disorder
back turns the two short words just given end to end

parts.note: to have a go is to try
lo is an old word for look

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word day's

explanation.surface: After a restless night, attempt to review the end of the day's caving.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEEP shuffled gives SPELE; GO and LO turned by 'back' give OLOG; then Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Speleology is the study and exploration of caves, which the British call potholing.

clue.text: Away from Hugh, sounded blue

parts.note: off means away from, as in off the road
the name Hugh, said out loud, is hue, which is another word for colour

explanation.surface: Someone spoke when apart from Hugh and felt down.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh sounds like 'hue', and a hue is a colour. 'blue' means risqué, not sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke that is off-colour is slightly indecent or risqué, and blue humour is the same.

clue.text: Risky game, changing our landlord right away

indicators.note: changing says the letters of our are rearranged
away means the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: A gamble on altering the terms with our landlord immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately'; it removes R from LETTER, leaving LETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: This casino game, betting on where a ball lands on a spinning wheel, is a classic gamble.

clue.text: Instrument not left over after more piccolos ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the remaining letters are put into a new arrangement
not means the letters for left and over are excluded

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is unused once extra piccolos have been bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music, with the piccolos; it is a lab tool. Take L and one O from MORE PICCOLOS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope is a scientific instrument for magnifying tiny objects.

clue.text: See 1
Cut tail off an amphibian

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: tail off means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a frog is an amphibian

explanation.surface: Chop the tail off a tadpole-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: An afro is a hairstyle, and a haircut can be called a cut.

clue.text: See 8
Failing to cross over to the other side

definitions.meaning: a failing is a fault or flaw

definitions.text: to cross over to the other side
definitions.meaning: to desert one's country or party and join the opposition

explanation.surface: Falling short when trying to get over to the far side.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a flaw; as a verb it means to abandon a side for its rival.

clue.text: Flipper frolics after heading off for a wave

indicators.note: frolics signals the remaining letters playing about into a new order
heading off means the first letter of Flipper is removed

explanation.surface: The TV dolphin Flipper plays about after swimming off, looking for a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes F, leaving LIPPER; 'frolics' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripple is a small wave on the surface of water.

clue.text: Paul and I cooked an Asian dish

indicators.note: cooked says the letters of Paul and I are mixed up, as ingredients are

explanation.surface: Two people made a South Asian meal together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is spiced rice cooked in stock, a dish from South Asia and the Middle East.

clue.text: Sub writer, reportedly a solitary type

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: a sub is a loan or advance, and Virginia Woolf is the writer

explanation.surface: A submarine writer, so people say, keeps to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sub' suggests a submarine or a sub-editor; it is a loan, as in an advance of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who prefers to act alone and avoid company is called by this idiom.

clue.text: See 11
Composer with one German cow

parts.note: Gustav Holst composed The Planets
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A composer and a German together own a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holstein is a breed of black-and-white dairy cattle.

clue.text: Horse leading lady got clipped

indicators.note: got clipped means the end of the word is trimmed off

parts.note: the heroine is the leading lady of a story

explanation.surface: The star actress had her horse groomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is a slang name for the drug, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse is street slang for this opiate drug.

clue.text: Shandy Man gets novelist back on the phone

indicators.note: on the phone means we only hear the words, so spelling may differ

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence was an English novelist; the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A man drinking shandy calls a novelist back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shandy' looks like the beer-and-lemonade drink; it is Tristram Shandy, the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote Tristram Shandy, so he is the man behind the eighteenth-century comic novel.
